title: Client-credit based SSE fragment resume protocol and client negotiation
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Background: We have recurring customer reports where long-running SSE streams drop and clients either lose partially-emitted tool/function-call frames or duplicate responses when reconnecting. Current resume tokens are server-centric and require exact event lineage; they fail when clients buffer partial fragments or when a proxy rewrites chunk boundaries. Goal: introduce a client-credit based resume protocol that lets clients (optionally) assert which fragments they have fully processed and request only missing fragments, combined with a compact fragment-credit header that is tolerant to re-framing and proxies. This ticket implements the runtime, compatibility shims for legacy JSONL streams, and tests for function-call/structured-output boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes new HTTP header X-RW-Fragment-Credits on SSE subscribe responses with initial credit window
Client can send X-RW-Ack-Fragment: <comma-separated fragment-ids> during reconnect to request delta replay
Server supports hybrid resume: accept either existing resume-token or fragment-credits header and reconcile coherently
No regression in canonical JSONL streaming clients (existing tests pass)
End-to-end tests cover function-call atomicity: reconnect cannot leave duplicated tool calls nor partial function call payloads in consumer-visible output
proposal_summary: Introduce a soft-resume layer above existing resume-token system. Clients maintain a small in-memory sliding window of fragment IDs (per stream). On reconnect they supply the highest contiguous fragment ID they hold plus an optional list of out-of-order fragments. Server computes minimal delta and streams only missing fragments. All fragments carry stable provenance headers (fragment-id, parent-epoch, toolcall-boundary flag). For legacy clients we fallback to resume-token semantics. For proxies that reframe chunks we include a lightweight fragment-checksum to detect reassembly mismatches and force server-side snapshot replay when needed.
implementation_notes: Server: add new FragmentManager to runtime with LRU retention of last 10k fragment metadata entries
HTTP: set initial window via response header X-RW-Fragment-Credits: 256
Reconnect: accept X-RW-Ack-Fragment in POST body or reconnect query param; negotiation prefers fragment-credit flow if both present
Backoff: server may reject resume request if fragments older than retention window; response includes Retry-After and resume-token fallback
Compatibility: add shim that maps old resume-token to equivalent fragment window when possible; otherwise fall back to full snapshot replay

Tool/Function-call boundaries: fragment metadata will include toolcall_start and toolcall_end flags; resume will not cut inside a flagged range - if client ack indicates interior cut, server will replay the whole toolcall payload
tradeoffs: Storage: keeping recent fragment metadata increases memory usage. We limit to 10k metadata items per stream and expose admission controls per customer tier
Complexity: fragment-credits adds negotiation complexity vs simple resume-token but reduces wasted replay for high-throughput low-latency clients
Proxy compatibility: not all proxies preserve custom headers; we keep resume-token fallback to maintain compatibility
Security: exposing fragment IDs and checksums may surface minor telemetry; ensure headers do not contain PII and are HMAC-signed for private deployments if KMS enabled
qa_plan: Unit tests for FragmentManager: insertion, eviction, delta computation
Integration tests: simulated partial-fragment disconnects with variable chunk reframe sizes (10B..8KB) via test harness
Chaos test: random TCP resets and proxy reframe in front of server to assert no duplicate function-call invocations
Performance: benchmark resume negotiation latency under 10k concurrent reconnects in staging
Compatibility: run legacy JSONL clients against runtime with header-based resume feature toggled off and on
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout: runtime flag 'fragment_resume_v1' default off
Canary deploy in us-west-2 baseline cluster with <= 10% traffic for 48h
If metrics stable, enable for dedicated customers with dedicated pools, then gradually for hosted customers
Provide SDK update with automatic fragment-credit bookkeeping (Node/Python) and backwards-compatible opt-in
monitoring_and_alerting: logging: include fragment-id and short checksum in trace spans for failed reconnections
risks: Fragment metadata retention pressure causing eviction leading to full snapshot replays for high fanout streams
Bugs in boundary flags could cause duplicate toolcalls or dropped structured outputs
Interoperability with third-party proxies that strip or mangle headers
open_questions: Should fragment checksums be HMACed for hosted customers by default? (security/ops input needed)
What is the correct retention SLA for low-tier customers? 1k fragments or 10k fragments?
Do we expose fragment window size controls in Console for Dedicated customers?
